pr.title: Spec an I don't understand action for every inbox item
pr.head: 5686bc9f743d7c09201f37f4701c612e62decd2c

summary: Projector's inbox holds the questions, notices, and requests that agents post for you. Projector's panel, above the Claude Code prompt, lists them, and each item's drawer shows its detail and the actions you can take, each on a digit key. When an item is written in the agent's shorthand, the only way to say you don't follow is discuss, which makes you type a sentence. For a notice, even that fails: a notice cannot be revised, and a reply to a subagent's notice never reaches that subagent.

This pull request adds a plan, inbox/unclear, at status ready and priority now. It specifies an I don't understand action on 6 in every open item's drawer. One press runs a new person-only command, project inbox unclear, which records unclear on the item. The panel then delivers UNCLEAR <number> <subject> to the posting agent, by the same claim-and-settle path that STARTED uses, and the agent revises the item in place. Notices become revisable, and a question's other options are capped at four so that 6 stays free. No code changes in this pull request.

The plan was written before #379 merged, and #379 lets a request carry up to five options of its own. The review's two open findings both come from that: on main, a request with a start action and five options already uses 6, and the agents block version the plan bumps to, 22, already shipped in #379.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Drawer: the panel area that opens under an inbox item, with its detail, choices, and actions.
  • Line owed: a message such as ANSWER, DISMISSED, or STARTED that the store records as waiting for delivery to the posting agent.
  • Claim: a deliverer's lease on the line an item owes, so that only one deliverer sends it.
  • Agents block: the versioned instructions that project init writes into a repository's AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.

cards.title: Drawer digits on main
cards.html:
DigitQuestionRequestNotice
1 to 6Up to six choicesStart on 1 when there is one, then up to five optionsFree
7discuss
8dismiss, or decline for a request
9snooze or unsnooze
0close the drawer

groups.title: The I don't understand plan
groups.kicker: A new nested plan under the completed inbox project
intro: The plan is the only file. Its sections follow the repository's plan layout: the problem, the solution with its flow, store, CLI, tools, and files, the reasons for the design, acceptance criteria, cost, rollout, and open questions.
Read it against main, not against the merge base. Main now includes #379, which changed how a request's drawer numbers its options and took agents block version 22.

checks.text: project show inbox/unclear --json and project check accept the plan at this head, its frontmatter matches what project create writes, and the parent inbox and inbox/requests plans are unchanged.
The only open question, the look of the action and its mark, has an owner and is deferred, so it does not block the ready status.

files.note: The whole plan: an I don't understand action on 6 that sends UNCLEAR to the posting agent and makes notices revisable.

checks.text: Open review finding: on main, a request with a start action and five options shows its fifth option on 6, because #379 numbers options from 2 after Start. The plan caps only a question's options and gives no fallback for a stored request that uses 6.
On main, revise refuses a notice with "withdraw it and tell again", and claim refuses every notice, as this section and § 2.3 say.
owed_line, claimed_line, claim, settle, and clear_for_outcome exist on main, and a claimed STARTED keeps its claim through an outcome, which is the behavior this section extends to unclear.

On main, ASK and ASKED in permissions.py list the person-only inbox commands. The module docstring, the CODEX_RULES comment, and two passages in docs/cli.md list them too, and the plan's files table does not name those.
Open review finding: agents block version 22 already shipped on main in #379, so the block needs version 23.

The start command guards against a stale drawer with --action. unclear takes no such guard, so a press that races a revision could mark the new text unclear. The revise tool redraws the item as soon as the CLI returns, so the window is narrow.
